binders: A finite index type ι, which is allowed to be empty.
A sample type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with the structure asserting that it is a probability measure.
A family X indexed by ι of real-valued functions X_i : Ω → ℝ.
A family of real coefficients a_i indexed by ι.
hypotheses: For every i in ι, X_i is measurable into the Borel measurable space on ℝ.
The indexed family (X_i) is jointly independent with respect to μ.
For every i in ι, the pushforward of μ by X_i is exactly the probability measure that assigns probability 1/2 to 1 and probability 1/2 to -1.
The threshold is strictly positive: 0 < t.
conclusions: The real-valued μ-measure of the event {ω ∈ Ω : |∑_{i∈ι} a_i X_i(ω)| ≥ t} is at most 2 exp(-t² / (2 ∑_{i∈ι} a_i²)).
mathematical_definitions: The common law of each X_i is obtained from a fair Boolean Bernoulli variable by mapping true to 1 and false to -1; equivalently, it is the symmetric Rademacher law on {-1, 1}.
Both sums are finite sums over every element of the Fintype ι.
The event is the two-sided tail event for the weighted sum S(ω) = ∑_{i∈ι} a_i X_i(ω).
The notation μ.real(A) means (μ(A)).toReal, the real conversion of the extended-nonnegative-real measure value.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any finite family of independent measurable real random variables on a probability space, if every variable has the symmetric Rademacher distribution taking 1 and -1 with equal probability, then for every choice of real coefficients and every positive real t, the probability that the absolute weighted sum |∑_i a_i X_i| is at least t is bounded above by 2 exp(-t²/(2∑_i a_i²)).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is only assumed finite, not nonempty. If it is empty, both finite sums are zero and the family-wise measurability, independence, and law hypotheses are vacuous.

The coefficients are arbitrary reals and may all be zero. Thus the denominator 2∑_i a_i² can be zero. Real division in Lean is totalized, so division by zero is defined (with inverse of zero equal to zero); in that case the displayed exponential factor evaluates using exponent 0 rather than being undefined.
The conclusion is stated only for strictly positive t.
The law hypothesis is exact equality of measures, not merely equality almost everywhere, matching moments, or support containment.
The family is indexed by a type rather than an ordered list; no ordering or distinctness assumption on coefficients or variables is present.

The left side uses Measure.real, i.e. ENNReal.toReal of the measure. For this probability measure the relevant values are finite, so the conversion has the usual probability value; outside finite-measure semantics, toReal at infinity would need care.
The theorem does not explicitly assume measurability of the tail event, but the separate measurability hypotheses on each X_i and finiteness of the sum supply the expected route to its measurability.
No centering, variance, boundedness, or almost-sure sign-valued hypotheses are stated separately; the exact common Rademacher law supplies the distributional content.
ambiguities: The one-level body shown for MeasureTheory.Measure.map is an opaque wrapper, so its exceptional behavior for a nonmeasurable map is not exposed in the dossier. This does not affect the stated case because measurability of every X_i is a separate hypothesis.

Several foundational structures are presented only by their types or inferred instances. Their standard mathematical readings are used above; no competing interpretation is suggested by the fully explicit target.
